known_issues.title: Beamos scorch marks last a few ticks longer
known_issues.detail: Hot_Floor 231 under a Beamos beam fades a few ticks later at 60: its own heat and fade are stepped as at 30 (the beam sets it each step, cLib_chaseF up 5 a tick while hit, down 0.4 after); the beam's half-step positions sweep a scorch once more than 30's whole-tick jumps do and add heat (finer sampling of the beam's path, like the water jar's edge): left as inherent (session bottom)

known_issues.title: A thrown water jar can break on an edge 30 misses
known_issues.detail: Dragon Roost room 8: thrown from about 100 units further back, the jar breaks on the floor's edge at 60 but in the lava at 30; 60's finer sampling catches an edge 30's step jumps over Decided (session bottom): inherent to the finer sampling (the jar moves on 30's ticks; its arc grazes the edge between two of them, where a 60 step lands), left.

known_issues.title: Ganon's Tower trial: the magma rocks' bob differs
known_issues.detail: The walk-in ends on 30's tick, and the rocks bob correctly on their own lava. The lava's bubbles come from the random stream, which parts from 30's before the warp: Outset's fishman picks his swim animation in a one-frame window that 30's ticks step over and 60's half steps land in, and his path is 0.7-1.6 units off from the start. After that every draw differs, so the bubbles do too. Not syncable: recorded (session bottom).

known_issues.title: Link: an action can change a tick off after his path drifts
known_issues.detail: Fixed: the turn in place and waiting start on 30's ticks; the turn while moving (a tick early), the swim's surfacing (a tick late) and a slash's next action (the spin's charge after a left slash, half a tick early) come on 30's ticks. Left: an action that starts at a threshold (a ledge reached, a turn's last 8000-unit step, a wall) can come a tick apart once his path is a few units or a degree off 30's, as in routes sidle and tour's corner

known_issues.title: Random-driven enemies drift from the 30 fps run
known_issues.detail: Random-driven enemies (Magtail waits, Peahat flights) drift from the 30 fps run, as expected

known_issues.title: Pots, sidling and ladders: fixed
known_issues.detail: Checked tick by tick at 30 and 60. Fixed: a thrown pot sank too fast in water (now within 0.2 units), sidling ran up to 2.3 units ahead (now on 30's ticks), sidling round a corner was stuck at 60 (now turns on 30's tick), a turn while carrying ended half a tick early (now on 30's tick), and lifting's hand-over to carrying came a tick late (fixed by Link's exact animation frame). Lifting, carrying, turning, walking and throwing a pot, and a ladder up and down, now match 30

known_issues.title: Windfall at night: the auction fixed
known_issues.detail: The lights converted (night via WWHD_DEBUG_TIME=905:345). The auction's bidders and the auction (361, 382) are 30's at every tick by night but for IDs given at their creation (session bottom); the bidding ran twice as fast at 60 and is now once a tick: the six bids and the choice on 30's ticks, the bid's call a tick early left (session top). Type 259, thought to be shutters, is Windfall's HD-only bunting line: its cloth never moves and it matches 30 every tick (session bottom)

known_issues.title: Enemies falling into water
known_issues.detail: Fixed for open water: at 60 the half step after an enemy reached the water went on sinking, so a Moblin ran 13.5 units deeper than 30's; now the tick ends at the surface as at 30, and Moblins and Bokoblins sink on 30's heights. The hang at the Outset dock's edge is the dock itself (30's Moblin is pushed out of its side for a tick), not the water check

queue_note: Round 14 (week 2, from 2026-10-09): performance for the Steam Deck and Android (B75), then the rival's lessons. Goal: full speed at 60 on the worker (power-capped, the Deck's stand-in); it reaches ~54 fps there with 3 CPU threads, GPU-bound. Two lanes, each worked from its top down: top (CPU side and turning the speed flags on by default) and bottom (GPU side, upscalers (FSR 1, then FSR 3.1/4, XeSS, DLSS: the owner's ask) and graphics options); main routes, deploys and keeps the docs; qa takes only problems the others are stuck on. Complexity 1-10 in brackets. On the owner's PC: ww-4 9385d6d.

queue.name: Round 14: [8] Three host threads by default (WWHD_CORES=3; 47 -> 54 fps on the worker): routes 3 against 1 on every predeploy route, a 1 h real-time soak, the locks list, per-core figures in the log; then on by default with full gates

Round 14: [4] Skip the title in test runs (the owner's ask): WWHD_DEBUG_BOOT=slot loads a save straight into play (no title, no file select), for the real-time routes, soaks and A/Bs (under load the title's fixed-frame press is missed and most runs replay); fallback: the press held until the file select shows; the deterministic checks keep the title (their reference has it)

Round 14: [3] Frame rate cap 30/40/50/60 in the settings (the owner's ask): 30 and 60 exact as today; 40 and 50 at 60 ticks' logic with a fixed pattern of dropped half-tick frames (keep-speed's machinery: full speed, slightly uneven motion, said in the option); smooth 40/50 comes with uncapped (D21 step 4); keep full speed always on in real time, no option (the owner, 2026-10-09)

Round 14: [5] Full speed below 30 (the owner's ask): when even whole-tick frames run late, skip their rendering too (the logic and actor draws still run, as keep-speed's dropped half frames), so a slow machine shows fewer frames at full speed; never skip a frame something reads back (the picto box, queries); a floor on frames shown; helps when rendering is the bottleneck (logic slower than 30 ticks a second can't keep speed)

Round 14: [7] The lazy GX2DrawDone by default (deck-plan item 2; -15% game thread): A/B on the desktop worker with a window, vsync on and off; a sync-validation run with it; then on by default with full gates

Round 14: [5] Variable refresh (the owner's ask: FreeSync / G-Sync Compatible / HDMI VRR): present so the display's VRR drives the refresh (the present mode, Linux's adaptive-sync hint; KDE, GNOME, gamescope, Windows fullscreen), frames paced by our own clock rather than vblank; a setting with a note when the display or compositor lacks it; dips and the 40/50 caps shown at their own rate; the owner tests on their monitor

Round 14: [5] Frame skipping's shown frames cost ~85 ms against ~48 ms in plain 30 (render-bound worker: 11.6 fps shown where ~20 should fit): find what piles into the shown frame (the GPU catching up, texture uploads) and fix it, so slow machines show as many frames as fit
Round 14: [6] Texture write-watch in real time (WWHD_WRITE_WATCH=1, deck-plan item 6): worker A/B of its gain, a soak with verify mode (0 misses), then on by default
Round 14: [9] A guest buffer cache (rival-study 9.3 #3): skip the per-frame vertex copy (~16% of the render thread) for buffers write-watch saw unchanged
Round 14: [6] 30 fps on the worker reaches only 27-28.7 fps: find where the time goes and fix it
Round 14: [9] The recompiled code itself (82% of the game thread, flat): registers kept in host registers, a real-time build without the cycle counting, -O3; measure each on the worker

Round 14: [3] An FPS overlay (the owner's ask): a display setting FPS overlay: off / FPS / FPS + frame time, applied at once, drawn in the bottom left corner over the picture after the upscaler (with frame generation: one number, the total shown including the generated frames, the owner's choice), readable at 4K (scaled with the display resolution), never in captures or the checks' images; its own panel beside frontend/overlay.cpp's (the keyboard and error panel), at a negligible cost

Round 14: [7] Scenes at other aspect ratios (the owner's ask, after b-wide): play the routes, cutscenes and menus at 4:3, 21:9 and 32:9 (and the Deck's 16:10) and list what breaks when the game shows more than its 16:9 frame: objects culled or popping in at the edges, cutscenes revealing what's off stage (actors waiting, unloaded or unfinished geometry, the sea's edge), screen effects and 2D overlays that cover only the middle (fades, wipes, the telescope, the Pictograph Box, maps), the menus (the owner's ask: the item menu and its item assignment, the map, the collection and quest screens, the pause and save screens, the GamePad screen shown on the TV: today their content is kept in the centred 16:9 with the background stretched, and the item buttons at the top right keep their 16:9 place; check each and decide centred or spread to the edges), the Pictograph Box working (the owner's ask: its viewfinder, a picture taken matches what the viewfinder showed, the saved pictograph's shape and how it shows in the album and the menus, the quests that judge a picture's subject (the Nintendo Gallery's figurines, Lenzo's) still pass or fail as at 16:9 with more view around it), fog, the sky and shadows at the edges, and Vert+ at 4:3 above and below. Then fix by kind: widen the culling, or show a cutscene at 16:9 with bars where it can't be fixed (as ultrawide mods do); findings in docs/research/, a capture per aspect
Round 14: [8] Uncapped U2: the tick rules at N (411), in parallel with U3

Round 14: [9] The pause menu (the owner's design, Pause Menu v9 from Claude Design; final in colour, type, size, motion and copy; the package on the worker, /wwhd/data/design/design_handoff_pause_menu_v9, its README the spec): M1 the UI layer (textured quads, the two OFL fonts rasterised at the scale s = min(w/1920, h/1080), the 1080p/2x PNGs; drawn over the presented picture, never into captures), the game held at the top of a whole tick while it's open (as a state save parks it: ask qa) over its blurred frame, the menu (Resume, Enhancements, Settings, Save, Quit), the cursor, the prompts for keyboard and pad, the Quit dialogs; M2 Settings on settings.cpp's options (Graphics, Display, Advanced, Diagnostics tabs, the info pane, Next-start banner, presets and Custom, the Deck's rules, planned options from the plan); M3 Save: the 4 state slots with thumbnails and their dialogs, File 1 through the game's own save, quit's unsaved check from the game's dirty flag; M4 Enhancements (the real list), the motion, 4K and the Deck's 1280x800. The debug menu stays the developers' own. Screenshots and the prototype's backdrop hold game frames: never in git

Round 14: [8] The start screen (the owner's design, Start Screen from Claude Design, after the pause menu and on its UI layer; partly after Dusklight's start menu; the package on the worker, /wwhd/data/design/design_handoff_start_screen, its README the spec; the name on screen is WindSong, never "WindSong HD"): S1 Launch: the game boots behind it and holds the title's first frame frozen as the backdrop (no still shipped), the menu (Start Game, Settings: the pause menu's screen, Game Files, Quit), Start releases the hold into the live title sequence; S2 Setup when no copy is registered: Browse (files .wua and an extracted folder with code/ content/ meta/; .wud/.wux only with their keys), drag and drop, checking with real progress (three steps remapped to the real phases), real validation (the title ID, USA v0 for now; others say so), wrong file, ready; the copy is read in place (registered path plus its verification in portable/), Change Files keeps the old copy until a new one verifies; Game Files with Re-verify; a pad-driven file browser for the Deck's Game Mode, where the system picker is unusable; S3 Android (with m-android A2): the touch layout at 1920x864, the Storage Access Framework (persistable URIs), system Back, no Quit, the pad switching to the desktop focus model, and a GPU driver step in Setup (System, or import a Turnip/Adreno package: m-android A4). Round 14: [8] A steady 144 and 165, the journal (the owner's go 2026-10-11): the desktop probe (en-tn, half frame median / p90 6.9 / 7.5-7.8 ms; journal off 5.4 / 6.0) puts the whole 1.5 ms in the journal: its per-half-frame setup, the rollback, and the stores into journaled pages (the census: of ~1.04M stores a half frame on en-tn, 72% near the stack and ~40k into journaled pages, ~43 pages written, 3.6k of them by other threads); cut each (page-protect isn't byte-exact); the stack-store skip (WWHD_STACK_SKIP, ~0.2 ms) only if it comes along free; target the half frame's p90 under 6.06 ms on the desktop, N 2 byte-identical as always

Round 14: [7] A steady 165, the draw side (after u8-journal): the whole frame's p90 is 6.7-7.1 ms on en-tn even with the journal off (a frame's draws cost a frame, whatever its step): the processes' draws (fpcM_Draw, 31% of a half frame) and RenderDisplay::draw's render lists (25%); profile them on the desktop, cut the exact wins, and measure each against 6.06 ms; N 2 byte-identical

Round 15: [6] The renderer on Android (m-android's GPU half, after u8/u9): what our Vulkan renderer requires (version, features: logicOp, depthClamp, geometryShader, BC textures, dualSrcBlend; extensions: transform feedback for streamout, custom border colour, dynamic rendering; limits; the host-visible ring) against the Odin's Adreno 740 under Qualcomm's driver and Turnip (their gpuinfo.org reports); a fallback chosen at device creation for each one missing, logged, never silent; each fallback testable on the desktop with a mask (WWHD_VK_MASK) and checked there with captures; the surface lost and recreated on Android's pause and resume (the swapchain remade on SDL's foreground events). The desktop byte-identical without a mask

Round 14: [9] Save states (the owner's ask, design approved 2026-10-11): save and load the whole game at the top of a whole tick (the main thread parked, the others in their OS waits, the clock frozen): game memory, thread contexts and the host-side records; a load boots fresh, parks at the same point, swaps the memory in, recreates the threads and flushes the renderer. M1 headless on the virtual clock, gated by determinism (save at swap N, load in a fresh run, actor states equal to the run that never stopped); M2 real time with Vulkan, audio and debug-menu slots, then a Deck test. For one-off repros like B16 first, testing second

Main starts A1 between deploys; A2 on goes to the first lane free. The worker's disk is at 93%: clean before the NDK and arm64 deps

Round 15: [5] Android speed, the game thread's host cost on the Odin (the owner's focus, 2026-10-14): kernel (the run queues' wakes, the scheduler lock), runtime, TLS; measured in play with tools/android/route.sh
Round 15: [5] Android speed, the GPU thread on the Odin: our renderer's per-draw cost (uniform uploads and zero fill, index copies, descriptors), measured in play
Round 15: [6] Android speed, the generated code's quality on arm64 (byte-swapped memory, unused CR/XER, spills, the yield check): fixes in tools/recomp that help x86 too

Round 15: [6] Android on a low-end device, the owner's Retroid Pocket 4 Pro (Dimensity 1100: A78 cores at 2.6 GHz, Mali-G77 on a Vulkan 1.1 driver with no dynamic rendering): first running at all (render passes standing in), then as fast as the Odin's work allows, without trading looks for speed

Round 15: [9] Graphics rework (the owner's ask, 2026-10-14): the game as good as the original or better, running better on low-end and high-end devices alike: never a look traded for speed. Research first (docs/research/graphics-rework.md), then the plan: not tweaks but whole systems, e.g. a native renderer of the game's scenes from its own draw structures instead of translating GX2 command streams draw by draw, our own shaders in place of the decompiled ones, batching and instancing, the same effects at a lower cost, render paths for tile-based mobile GPUs; each step measured on the Odin and the Deck class, and compared with the original's picture

Round 15: [9] No Cemu (the owner's ask, 2026-10-14): research first (docs/research/no-cemu-plan.md): every part of Cemu the program still builds, links or reads (OS libraries and our forks, Latte's shader decompiler, texture and address code, audio, config, logging, the vcpkg manifest, resources and game profiles, names), then the plan to replace each with our own until nothing named Cemu is built, linked or shipped
Round 15: [8] Windows port: the survey is done (docs/research/windows-plan.md); parked behind Android speed (the owner's choice, 2026-10-14)

later: FSR 4 (parked 2026-10-10 after bottom's evaluation): AMD ships it only as a signed DirectX 12 DLL (SDK 2.3); the community Vulkan ports use a leaked model we can't ship. Waiting for AMD's Vulkan FSR 4; FSR 3.1's inputs (HUD split, motion, jitter) fit it; revisit at each SDK release
XeSS (parked 2026-10-10): Intel ships it only as closed Windows DLLs (no Linux library); for the Windows platform work, on FSR 3.1's inputs

DLSS (parked 2026-10-10, the owner's call): NVIDIA's RTX SDK licence forbids its files in our public repo (distribution only as object code; not under an open-source licence); a compliant route exists (nothing NVIDIA in git, an optional local SDK path at build time, our glue code under MPL); needs an NVIDIA GPU to test

Optimised shaders (parked 2026-10-10 after bottom's measurements on the worker): exact branch-free multiply +0.5% (noise), SPIRV-Tools -O +1.9% (noise), even inexact a*b only -5%: the iGPU is bandwidth-bound, which render scale answers. Revisit on an ALU-bound GPU (phones, the Android port)

The half step's journal inline check in RT_STORE (parked 2026-10-10 after top's A/B: exact, but no gain on the worker, +0.3% mixed: the bigger store sites cost what the saved calls did; on top's local branch)
Platforms: Linux arm64, Windows, Android and CI through cloud sessions on github.com/flossbud/WWHDRecomp (docs/cloud-handoff.md)
Android-specific speed: ADPF hints, core pinning, thermal (deck-plan), once the port runs
More of the rival's lessons (rival-study 9.3): save states, a constant guest memory base, draw batching, interpolation as a low-power mode
The owner's extensive testing and repair
Uncapped U7 (uncapped-plan.md): N chosen per tick from the frame time; the owner: whatever works best, so decided once U5's fixed rates run
